new.text: 7.8 BSW Error Handling Beside application software components also the basic software (BSW) can detect errors (e.g. hardware driver faults), especially during startup (ref. to document [11] for further details). For these errors (only a small number compared to application specific events), some additional aspects apply: • Errors can be detected at startup before Dem is fully initialized • Errors can be reported during startup, information needs to be buffered until Dem is fully available • Errors can be reported between startup and shutdown, information needs to be buffered and need to be processed by the Dem main function (RTE related call tree requirement) • Entries in the event memory can have a different configuration (e.g. no empha- sis on freeze frame data for the workshop) Dem_SetEventStatus is used by BSW modules to report errors from the point in time when the Dem module is pre-initialized. Within Dem_Init, the queued events are processed. During normal operation (after full initialization), the queuing mechanism of the API Dem_SetEventStatus is necessary to process the reported fault within the main function of the Dem module. Dem_SetEventStatus can be used by BSW modules to report errors from the point in time when the Dem module is pre-initialized. Within Dem_Init, the queued events are processed. new.text: 7.11.5.1 Initialize NvM Data Reprogramming of an ECU with an updated DEM configuration may lead to inconsis- tencies of the integrity and validity of Dem related data stored in NvM. (e.g. Ids stored in non-volatile Dem related data might not match to the reprogrammed DEM configu- ration) Dem is providing the functions Dem_InitAllNvmBlocks and Dem_InitAllNvm- BlocksGetResult to support a non-AUTOSAR-specified handler/manager to resolve those validity issues by initializing all Dem related NvM data blocks. [SWS_Dem_01420] Acceptance of Requests During the Valid Initialization Se- quence Upstream requirements: RS_Diag_04211 ⌈If the function Dem_InitAllNvmBlocks is called after Dem_PreInit and before Dem_Init, the Dem shall accept the request and return E_OK.⌋ [SWS_Dem_01421] Handling of Requests Outside the Valid Initialization Se- quence Upstream requirements: RS_Diag_04211 ⌈If the function Dem_InitAllNvmBlocks is called before Dem_PreInit or after Dem_Init, the Dem shall not accept the request and shall return E_NOT_OK.⌋ [SWS_Dem_01422] Initialization and Storage Actions for Accepted Non-Volatile Memory Requests Upstream requirements: RS_Diag_04211 ⌈If a Dem_InitAllNvmBlocks request was accepted before Dem_Init, the Dem shall do the following actions during execution of Dem_Init: • Reset the volatile data buffers of all the Dem related NvM data blocks to initial values. • Trigger an immediate NvM storage request to store the updated volatile data buffers in NvM. ⌋ [SWS_Dem_01423] Successful Completion of Non-Volatile Memory Initialization and Storage Upstream requirements: RS_Diag_04211 ⌈The function Dem_InitAllNvmBlocksGetResult shall return E_OK if the function Dem_InitAllNvmBlocks was called successfully and all Dem related NvM blocks are initialized and stored to non-volatile memory.⌋ [SWS_Dem_01424] Indication of Ongoing Non-Volatile Memory Storage Upstream requirements: RS_Diag_04211 ⌈The function Dem_InitAllNvmBlocksGetResult shall return E_PENDING if the function Dem_InitAllNvmBlocks was called successfully, but storing to non-volatile memory is still ongoing and not yet finished.⌋ [SWS_Dem_01425] Error Indication for Unsuccessful or Invalid Non-Volatile Memory Operations Upstream requirements: RS_Diag_04211 ⌈The function Dem_InitAllNvmBlocksGetResult shall return E_NOT_OK in all other cases. (e.g. when Dem_InitAllNvmBlocks was not called successfully or Dem related NvM storage operations are returning an error)⌋
